name: Ecaterina Szabo
milestone_by_age_26: Won four gold medals and one silver at the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics at age 16, becoming the most successful athlete of the Games.
early_history_summary: Szabo started gymnastics at age five at the Gymnastics School in Onești, Romania, and was identified early as a major talent. She won the Junior European all-around title in 1980 at age 12 and defended it in 1982, becoming the first gymnast to do so. By 15, she was winning medals at the senior World Championships, and at 16, she won four gold medals at the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics.
family_context_summary: Born to ethnic Hungarian parents in Zagon, Transylvania, Romania; her given name Katalin was changed to Ecaterina by Romanian authorities to obscure her Hungarian background.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Onești gymnastics school, Károlyi coaches, Romanian gymnastics system, early specialization, ethnic Hungarian minority
evidence_summary: Szabo's gymnastics career was built on Romania's elite gymnastics pipeline, starting at the Gymnastics School in Onești at age five under coaches Maria Cosma and Mihai Agoston. She was later coached by the legendary Béla and Márta Károlyi before their defection, then by Adrian Goreac at Cetate Deva. Her physical talent was extraordinary: she won Junior European all-around titles at 12 and 14, and scored perfect 10s at the World Championships at 15. As an ethnic Hungarian in Romania, her name and birthdate were altered by authorities, adding a layer of institutional adversity to her path.
